families.name: single-booking
families.tests: One booking request the booking node can serve on its own, across the whole of its range: who the practitioners are and whether one with a given specialty is on the roster, when one is free, what this patient already holds, and the three writes. A write is confirmed before it happens, so those cases carry a scripted second turn - including bare affirmatives, which must read as the booking they answer and never as small talk. One case carries history instead, for the turn that names no practitioner at all and is answerable only by carrying one forward from an earlier message. Every case states the appointments the patient must hold when it ends.

cases.message: Which practitioners do you have?
Do you have a dentist?

requests.gist: is there a dentist on the roster

cases.message: Do you have a cardiologist I could see?
cases.note: the roster holds a GP and a dentist only, so the honest answer is no - the case is here to catch a confabulated yes, and nothing is booked

cases.message: What times does William Osler have free on Wednesday?
When could I see the dentist on Tuesday morning?
cases.note: names a specialty rather than a person, so the roster has to be read before times can be offered

cases.message: Is there anything free on Saturday?

history.text: I would like to get a tooth filling.
Of course - which day would suit you?

requests.gist: Saturday availability for the dental visit

cases.note: the message itself names neither a practitioner nor a specialty: 'tooth filling' is in the history, so the turn is only answerable by carrying it forward. Only the dentist works Saturday and the GP's week ends Friday, so a reply offering a GP slot is wrong twice over. The clinic's own turn names neither the dentist nor dentistry, so the resolution has to come from the patient's words rather than from a specialty the assistant already said out loud

cases.message: Book me in with William Osler on Wednesday at 10am.

requests.gist: book a named practitioner at a named time

cases.note: one slot is on the table, so the bare 'OK' can only be confirming it - the small-talk reading would leave nothing booked

cases.message: I need a dental appointment on Tuesday morning, please.

scheduling.reply: The earliest of those works - please book it.

cases.note: no time named, so the reply picks from what was offered and the expectation names the day only

cases.message: When is my next appointment?
cases.note: a read: the appointment must still stand, unchanged, afterwards

cases.message: What appointments do I have booked?
cases.note: two standing appointments, so a reply naming one of them is short

cases.message: Can you move my Thursday appointment to Friday at 12?
cases.note: a moved appointment is the same appointment: the Thursday slot must not survive beside the Friday one

cases.message: Please cancel my appointment tomorrow.
Could I push my dentist visit back a couple of hours?

requests.gist: move the dental visit later the same day

cases.note: the new time is relative and unstated, so the second turn is what fixes it; 11:00 is inside the dentist's 09:00-14:00 day

families.name: urgent_condition
families.tests: A message describing something an emergency department exists for. It takes the whole turn, whatever else it is wrapped in: the reply is the fixed text pointing at emergency services, a person is called, and the assistant falls silent. The assistant does not triage, so no case here expects a judgement about severity.

cases.message: I have chest pain radiating down my arm, what should I do?

requests.gist: chest pain radiating to the arm

cases.message: I can't breathe properly.
I think I'm having a heart attack.
I've taken too many of my tablets.
My tooth is absolutely killing me, I need to be seen.
cases.note: the counter-case: everyday hyperbole about an ordinary complaint is a booking, not an emergency. Pairs with G-b-01 to stop the label being won by pain words alone

families.name: distress
families.tests: Real fear, panic or acute upset about the patient's health or care, whether or not the message asks for anything. It calls a person and stops the assistant. A brief exclamation is small talk instead, so the family carries that counter-case too.

cases.message: I'm terrified about my results.
I am so frightened that something is seriously wrong with me.
Ugh, what a week.
cases.note: the counter-case: a brief exclamation is not distress, and paging a person for it is the queue noise the distress label must not create

families.name: booking_for_another
families.tests: The message says plainly that the appointment is for someone other than the person in this chat, which is an authority question a person has to settle. It covers a change as well as a new booking. The third party must be the one the appointment is FOR: merely naming another person is an ordinary booking, which the counter-case carries - and that is the only case here with a scheduling fixture, since a handed-off turn writes nothing.

cases.message: Can I book Monday for my mother?
I'm calling on behalf of my father, he needs an appointment.

requests.gist: booking on behalf of a parent

cases.message: Can I cancel my wife's Thursday appointment?
cases.note: a change for someone else is this too, not just a new booking

cases.message: My wife recommended you - can I book myself in for Tuesday with dr. Andreas?
cases.note: the counter-case: the appointment is for the person in the chat, so naming a third party does not make it theirs

families.name: not_authorized
families.tests: A real request that the assistant may never serve, whatever the corpus grows to hold - a sick note, a prescription, a records transfer, money. It makes no search and no generation call: the patient gets the fixed notice and a person is called under a cause distinct from a corpus gap, because one is fixed by writing an entry and the other by nothing. It does not silence the assistant.

cases.message: I'd like you to write me a sick note for my employer.
Can you renew my prescription?
There's a mistake on my bill, please correct it.
Send my records over to another clinic.
Can you refund my last visit?
Can you tell me what my blood test results mean?
I need a copy of my vaccination certificate.
Please change the name on my file to my married name.
How long does a refund usually take?
cases.note: the counter-case: asking how a policy works is a question, not a request for an action - faq_question, and a gap in this corpus

families.name: call_staff
families.tests: An explicit request for a human, and nothing else. It is the one cause that owes the patient silence afterwards, so the assistant stops. The label must not collect the staff-handled issues that have causes of their own - a billing problem is not_authorized, an emergency is urgent_condition.

cases.message: I'd rather speak to a person.
Put me through to the front desk, please.
You said you could put me through to someone about my coverage - please do that.

history.text: We accept most major insurance providers, including Blue Cross Blue Shield, Aetna, Cigna, UnitedHealthcare, and Medicare. If you're unsure whether your specific plan is covered, you can ask me to connect you with a member of our friendly front desk team.

requests.gist: takes up the offer across turns

cases.note: the insurance entry offers to connect the patient with the front desk, and this is a patient taking that offer up a turn later - the shape the entry actually produces - so the reply has to route to a person rather than answer again

cases.message: Is there someone I can talk to about all this?

families.name: small-talk
families.tests: Messages that ask for nothing the clinic could act on: greetings, thanks, acknowledgements, farewells, thinking it over, gibberish. The point of the family is that none of them pages a person and none of them searches the corpus - before the label existed, 'Thanks' retrieved, abstained and called a human. Several carry history, because a bare acknowledgement only reads as one against the turn it answers.

cases.message: Hi
Thanks!
cases.note: the request in the history has its answer after it, so the thanks thanks the clinic rather than trailing something still open

cases.message: OK

history.text: Please arrive 15 minutes before your appointment time.

cases.note: an acknowledgement of an answered question. The same word after an offered slot would be a booking (G-a-08), which is why both exist

cases.message: Sure

history.text: We are open Monday through Saturday, 9am to 6pm.

cases.note: nothing was asked of the patient, so 'Sure' agrees with nothing and is not a confirmation

cases.message: Bye
asdfgh
Merci
Let me think about it a bit.

families.name: out-of-topic
families.tests: A question clearly outside the clinic's domain. It does request something, so an earlier rule made it an escalation - and paging a person because a patient asked about the weather is exactly the queue noise escalation must not carry. There is nothing for staff to do and nothing in the corpus to find, so it is answered politely as small talk and calls nobody.

cases.message: Who won the football last night?
What's the weather in Paris today?

families.name: single-faq-answered
families.tests: One FAQ question the pinned corpus answers. The whole RAG path has to work: the request clears the similarity floor and the rerank floor, an answer is generated from what was retrieved, and the citation points at the entry that actually carries it. Several are deliberate paraphrases sharing no wording with their entry, so the family measures retrieval rather than string overlap.

cases.message: What should I bring to my first appointment?
What are your opening hours?
Where are you based?
Can I see a specialist if my GP hasn't sent anything over?
cases.note: a paraphrase sharing no wording with the entry, and phrased as a 'can I see' question that must not be read as an availability check

cases.message: Is it possible to have my appointment over video call?
cases.note: the corpus answers no; the case is here to check a no is given rather than abstained on

cases.message: Do you take Aetna?
cases.note: the entry lists the plans it accepts, and this names one of them, so the answer has to settle a membership question rather than repeat the list back

cases.message: Is there anywhere to park near the clinic?
How much is a dentist visit if I'm paying myself?
Can I pay with my HSA card?
What happens if you don't take my insurance?
How long before my slot should I turn up if I've been before?
cases.note: the entry answers first visits and returning patients differently, so an answer giving only the 15-minute figure is wrong

families.name: single-faq-gap
families.tests: One FAQ question the pinned corpus cannot answer. These are near misses: they sound like clinic policy and most of them overlap an entry heavily in vocabulary, so the retrieval will surface something plausible. The system must abstain and raise a corpus gap rather than stretch a neighbouring entry into an answer - a stretched answer is a confident false statement to a patient. The last two name the very things an entry lists and ask about a combination of them, which is the wording a gap is likeliest to carry through both gates on - they cover the region where generation is the only step left to notice the corpus does not answer. Whether a given one is stopped at the rerank floor or reaches generation is a property of the build, not of the case.

cases.message: How much does an MRI scan cost out of pocket?
cases.note: heavy overlap with the rates entry, which prices a GP, a dentist and 'other specialist consultations' - not a scan

cases.message: Is the entrance wheelchair accessible?
cases.note: entirely plausible clinic policy, absent from the corpus

cases.message: Can I pay by cheque?
cases.note: the payment entry lists cash, cards and FSA/HSA. A list that does not mention cheques is not an answer about cheques

cases.message: What is your cancellation and no-show policy?
cases.note: asks the terms governing a cancellation, which the records do not hold either - it must not reach the booking node

cases.message: Do I need to fast before a blood test?
Are you open on public holidays?
cases.note: same subject as the hours entry, which gives weekdays only and says nothing about holidays

cases.message: How much is a follow-up visit?
cases.note: same subject as the rates entry, which prices first visits by practitioner type and never distinguishes a follow-up

cases.message: Do you accept UnitedHealthcare and Blue Cross Blue Shield for the same visit, splitting the cost between them?

requests.gist: splitting a visit's cost between two insurers

cases.note: the entry lists both insurers among those accepted and says nothing about dividing one bill between two of them. It is phrased as the entry's own question so it carries through the rerank gate rather than being stopped there: the narrative wording this case had first - 'my policy will soon be switched to ... is it possible to split the cost?' - scored 0.463 against a floor of 0.58 and never reached generation, which is not the region the case is for

cases.message: Can I pay half with my HSA card and half in cash for the same visit?

requests.gist: splitting one visit's payment across two methods

cases.note: the same shape against the payment entry, which names cash and HSA cards among the methods accepted and says nothing about dividing one payment between two of them. It also guards the group-to-member licence in the generation prompt: accepting each method separately is not accepting them combined

families.name: single-faq-that-looks-multi
families.tests: One request wearing the clothes of several: a list of options, an aside in the middle of one, two phrasings of one question. The classifier must not over-split them. Splitting here is not harmless - each half retrieves separately and competes for the same shortlist, and the reply then answers one question twice instead of answering it once.

cases.message: Can I pay with an HSA card, or a Visa, or cash? Any of those?
cases.note: one request listing options, answered from one entry once

cases.message: So, my insurance is Blue Cross, and I was wondering, because my last clinic did not take it, whether you do?
cases.note: comma-heavy with an aside, still one request

cases.message: Do you do walk-ins? Can I just turn up without an appointment?
cases.note: two phrasings of one request, and a gap - so an over-split shows up as two abstentions and two gap escalations for one question

families.name: compound-faq-answered
families.tests: Two or three FAQ questions in one message, every one of them answerable. The retrieval pipeline runs once per request and is never pooled: under a shared shortlist the stronger question crowds the other out, and the weaker one abstains for no reason but its company. Each request carries its own citations, so a case answered from one entry twice cites that entry twice.

cases.message: What are your opening hours, and what should I bring to my first visit?
How early should I arrive, and which insurance plans do you accept?
When is payment due, and what cards do you take?
cases.note: both answered from one entry, so it is cited once per request - two citations of the same chunk, not one deduplicated across the turn

cases.message: Do I need a referral, do you take Cigna, and when do I pay?
cases.note: three requests, which is the segment cap - nothing may be dropped and cap_bound must stay false, since three that fit is not a message cut short

cases.message: What if you don't take my insurance, and how much is a GP visit then?
cases.note: the second request depends on the first's answer and still stands alone once restated

families.name: compound-faq-mixed
families.tests: Two requests in one message, each reporting its own verdict - so there is no single value describing the turn. Most pair an answerable half with a gap, and the reply must answer the half it can and name the half it cannot without blurring them: never soften the gap into a partial answer, never stretch the answer to cover it. One pairs an answerable half with a request the assistant may never serve, a different cause needing a different fix. One is a gap twice over, where every request abstains and the turn collapses to the fixed abstention text with no composing call, still reporting an outcome per request. The hardest are the pairs sharing a subject, where the entry retrieved for the answerable half is also the nearest miss for the gap.

cases.message: What are your clinic hours, and do you validate parking?
cases.note: same entry is the evidence for one half and the near miss for the other

cases.message: Do you offer telehealth, and is the clinic wheelchair accessible?
Do you see children under five, and what are your opening hours?
cases.note: the gap comes FIRST, so the reply must not let the answered half absorb it - the order is part of what is being tested

cases.message: What is the out-of-pocket rate for a specialist, and is a scan included?
cases.note: one subject, split answerability - the same entry both answers and fails to answer, which is the hardest kind not to blur

cases.message: Do I need a referral to see a specialist, and can you renew my prescription?
cases.note: the second half is not a corpus gap - no entry could ever make the assistant able to renew a prescription. Different cause, different fix, and the answered half still runs

cases.message: Do you validate parking, and how much does an MRI scan cost if I pay myself?
cases.note: neither half is answerable, so every request abstains and the turn takes the collapse path - one fixed abstention text, no composing call, and still one outcome per request. Each half is a near miss on a different entry: the hours entry names the garage, the rates entry prices a GP, a dentist and other consultations but no scan. Both wordings ask what the clinic's policy is rather than asking it to act, which is what keeps them faq_question and off the not_authorized side

families.name: request-segmentation
families.tests: Requests that cannot be searched or answered as written: they borrow a subject from an earlier clause, or refer back with a pronoun or an ellipsis - and one borrows from the previous turn rather than from anything in its own message. Each piece has to be restated so it stands alone - 'and how much is the visit?' has to become 'how much is a dentist visit?' or it retrieves against nothing. Restating must not add: a resolved reference keeps what was asked, and inventing the constraint that decides the answer is worse than dropping it.

cases.message: When is a dentist available on Tuesday morning, and how much is the visit if I'm paying out of pocket?
cases.note: the second request has to carry 'dentist' across from the first, or it asks the price of nothing in particular - and the rates entry prices a dentist differently from a GP, so the restatement decides the answer

cases.message: Do I need a referral? And what about for a dentist?

requests.gist: is a referral needed for a dentist

cases.note: ellipsis: the second clause has no verb of its own

cases.message: Do you have parking, and is it free?
cases.note: 'is it free?' cannot be searched as written

cases.message: And a dentist?

history.text: How much is a GP visit if I'm paying out of pocket?

cases.note: the reference reaches back a turn rather than a clause: the message carries no verb, no price word and no way to be searched as written, so everything that makes it a question comes from the conversation. The assistant's turn gives the GP figure only, so the dentist's price has to be retrieved rather than read back out of the history - and the entry prices the two differently, so the restatement decides the answer

cases.message: Do you take Medicare? What if you don't take my plan?
cases.note: the second request is conditional on the first's answer and still stands alone; the two rest on different entries

families.name: pleasantry-plus-request
families.tests: A greeting, a thank-you or an acknowledgement attached to a real request. The pleasantry must not hide the request, and it is not a segment of its own: it is left out rather than folded in, so the turn carries exactly the requests that were made. The request behind it is drawn from every route - FAQ, a booking read, a booking write, and a call for a person.

cases.message: Morning - what should I bring to a first visit?
Thanks! Any slots with William Osler on Wednesday?
Hi, I need to cancel tomorrow.
cases.note: a greeting in front of a write: the appointment must still be cancelled at the end

cases.message: Cheers - when is my next appointment?
Thanks, but I'd rather speak to someone.
cases.note: the pleasantry sits in front of a cause that stops the turn

cases.message: Perfect. What time should I arrive?

history.text: Your appointment with Dr. Osler is booked for Wednesday at noon.

cases.note: 'Perfect.' acknowledges the confirmation and the question follows from it. A turn read as small talk here answers nothing

families.name: mixed-faq-booking
families.tests: One FAQ half and one booking half in a single message. Each specialist is handed only its own segment, so the other half's clause is not in the prompt to be answered: a booking node that sees the policy question may answer it from nothing, and a retrieval that sees the booking clause searches the corpus for live data it does not hold. Every case's booking half has to leave the scheduler in a stated state, so a turn that answers the question and quietly drops the booking fails.

cases.message: What should I bring, and can you book me Wednesday at 9 with William Osler?
cases.note: the booking half names a practitioner and a time, so the bare 'OK' confirms one slot

cases.message: Which insurers do you accept, and which practitioners do you have?
cases.note: two list questions, one answered from the corpus and one from the records - the pair a pooled retrieval would answer from one place

cases.message: How much is a GP visit if I'm paying cash, and could I see one on Wednesday morning?
cases.note: the booking half names no practitioner - 'one' stands for the GP in the other clause, so the restatement has to carry the specialty across, and the GP resolves to one person on the roster. It read 'is there anything free on Wednesday morning?' until the specialty failed to cross: that clause is complete as written and asks about any practitioner, so inserting GP would have been the constraint rule (3) forbids inventing rather than an ellipsis rule (2) resolves

cases.message: What is your address, and can you move my Wednesday visit to the same time next week?
cases.note: 'the same time next week' is +9d from a Monday clock
